initial_requirements: Pecan Springs Elementary School needs a web-based learning game that helps sixth-grade students improve their fraction-solving skills. Students should answer fraction questions as part of an interactive game and receive feedback based on their performance. The project should also provide a common web menu through which students and teachers can access Space Fractions alongside related educational games.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What core actions and feedback should Space Fractions provide for sixth-grade students during gameplay—for example, how should they answer fraction questions, what kinds of hints or corrections should appear, and what should happen when they complete a level or make repeated mistakes?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
Students should be able to select or enter an answer to each fraction question in a simple, game-like way, and the system should tell them right away whether they’re correct. If they miss a question, it should give a short hint or show the correct method rather than just saying “wrong,” so they can try again and understand the mistake.
If they keep making the same kind of mistake, I’d want the game to give a more guided correction or an easier prompt, so they don’t get stuck. When they complete a level, it should give positive feedback, show their progress, and move them into the next challenge or award some kind of game reward.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Who are the different users or stakeholder groups who will use or manage Space Fractions, and what should each group be able to do in the system?
turns.interviewee_utterance: The main groups are students, teachers, and school staff who manage the web menu or game access. Students should be able to play Space Fractions and see their feedback and progress, while teachers should be able to assign or launch the game and review how students are doing. For the school side, someone should be able to maintain the common menu and make sure Space Fractions is available alongside the other educational games.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What specific rules should govern gameplay and progression in Space Fractions—for example, how many questions or attempts are needed to complete a level, when should the game offer hints or easier prompts, and are there any scoring, reward, or advancement rules teachers or the school want enforced?
turns.interviewee_utterance: I don’t have the exact numbers locked down yet, like how many questions make up a level or how many attempts count before a hint appears. What we do know is that the game should reward correct work, give help when students struggle, and let them move forward once they’ve shown they understand the skill for that level. If teachers or the school want specific scoring or advancement rules enforced, I’d need to check with them before I could say for sure.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What student, gameplay, or progress data should Space Fractions store or display—for example, answers, scores, hint usage, level completion, teacher assignments, or per-student progress—and are there any data fields you need tracked for reporting or classroom review?
turns.interviewee_utterance: We’d want it to store and show the basics like each student’s answers, whether they were correct, their score or progress through the game, and which levels they’ve completed. It would also be useful to track hint usage and repeated mistakes so teachers can see where students are struggling. For classroom review, per-student progress and completion history would be the most important, but I’d need to confirm whether we want anything beyond that, like time spent or detailed reporting fields.

turns.interviewer_utterance: For the common web menu, how should students, teachers, and school staff navigate to Space Fractions and the other educational games, and what access or permissions should each user type have when using that menu?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Students should be able to open the common menu, pick Space Fractions, and go straight into the game without dealing with anything complicated. Teachers should have access to the same menu but also be able to view student-related options, like launching activities or checking progress, if that’s part of the system. School staff who manage the menu should be able to add, remove, or reorder the games and control which links are visible to each group.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Are there any technical, instructional, or operational constraints we should design Space Fractions around—for example required devices or browsers, school network limitations, accessibility needs, login or privacy requirements, or any rules about how the game can be deployed and used in the classroom?
turns.interviewee_utterance: We do need it to be web-based so it can run on school devices without special software, but I don’t have a confirmed list of browsers or devices yet. It should work well in a classroom setting, so it needs to be simple to use, reasonably fast, and appropriate for sixth graders, with accessibility in mind if possible. On login and privacy, I’d need to check with the school’s policies before committing to any specific requirements, because that part hasn’t been decided yet.

slots.name: project_goals
slots.value: Help sixth-grade students at Pecan Springs Elementary improve fraction-solving skills through a web-based learning game, with interactive gameplay, immediate feedback, progress tracking, and rewards/next challenges.

slots.name: stakeholder_roles
slots.value: Students play Space Fractions and view feedback/progress; teachers can launch or assign activities and review student performance; school staff maintain the common web menu, manage game access, and ensure Space Fractions is available alongside other educational games.

slots.name: functional_needs
slots.value: Students must be able to select or enter answers to fraction questions in a simple game-like interface; the system must provide immediate correctness feedback, short hints or correct-method guidance on mistakes, more guided correction or easier prompts for repeated errors, and positive completion feedback with progress display and advancement to the next challenge or reward.

slots.name: business_rules
slots.value: Exact level size, attempt limits, scoring thresholds, and advancement rules are not yet defined. The game should reward correct work, provide help when students struggle, and allow progression once students demonstrate understanding of the level's skill.

slots.name: data_entities
slots.value: The system should store and display student answers, whether each answer was correct, scores or progress through the game, completed levels, hint usage, repeated mistakes, per-student progress, and completion history.

slots.name: constraints
slots.value: The game must be web-based so it can run on school devices without special software. It should work well in a classroom setting, be simple to use, reasonably fast, and appropriate for sixth graders, with accessibility in mind if possible. Specific browser/device support and login/privacy requirements are not yet confirmed and must be checked against school policy.

slots.name: quality_concerns
slots.value: The system should be easy for sixth graders to use, perform well enough for classroom use, and include accessibility considerations. Reliability and smooth access through the web menu are also important.

slots.name: common_web_menu_navigation
slots.value: Students should be able to open the common web menu, select Space Fractions, and enter the game without complexity; teachers should access the same menu and may have student-related options such as launching activities or checking progress; school staff should be able to manage the menu by adding, removing, or reordering games and controlling which links are visible to each user group.

slots.name: integration_with_other_educational_games
slots.value: Space Fractions must be listed alongside other educational games in a shared common web menu, with the menu managed so the game is visible and accessible to the appropriate user groups.

slots.name: access_control_by_user_type
slots.value: Students can access the menu and launch Space Fractions; teachers can access the menu and may also see student-related options such as launching activities and checking progress; school staff can manage menu content and control which game links are visible to each user group.

slots.name: student_progress_visibility_scope
slots.value: Students should see their own feedback and progress in the game. Teachers should be able to review how students are doing, including per-student progress and completion history for classroom review.
